Verified again on 2026-09-21 by the bundle-kind/speciation lane over spec.example.toml and the codex/bio-wiring-20260915 source branch: no pH-dependent rate law exists on either. Writing one would be inventing a law, which the lane brief forbids, so this row STOPS here. The screening half of the old entry is also still unbuildable: no relation kind carries a charge, and giving one a charge is a resolution decision (see the bound), not a missing line of code
detail.bound: E' P2 / P3, two numbers. (i) SCREENING: at chem.ionic_strength 150 mM the Debye length is 0.8 nm — 1/56 of the SHORTEST interaction reach in the spec (erm.reach 45 nm) and 1/62 of resolution.spacing, so a screened term is exp(-56) = 3.7e-25 of an unscreened one at the closest distance this model resolves. (ii) SPECIATION, kept as the PREDICTION the device run is compared with now that the law is BUILT: at chem.mg_free 500 uM and chem.mgatp_kd 100 uM (a spec row since 2026-09-21; it was literature-only when this bound was written), [MgATP] is 0.8333 x chem.atp_conc, so the ATP-binding edge runs at 2500 /s instead of 3000 /s and the crossbridge cycle time 0.486 s (sum of 1/k_adp_release, 1/k_stroke, 1/k_pi_release, 1/k_hydrolysis, 1/(k_atp_bind x atp_conc)) lengthens by 0.014 %; even at a 10x weaker Kd of 1000 uM it is 0.137 %
detail.verdict: SMALL FOR THIS ENGINE — the screened term is below floating-point at the model's own resolution, and Mg-ATP speciation (now BUILT) moves the crossbridge cycle by 0.014 % (0.14 % at a 10x weaker Kd), far inside the spread the rate rows already declare. The honesty this number does NOT buy: chem.mg_free and chem.ph are often called "the conditions the rates were measured at", and reading the sources says otherwise — of the 10 SOURCED rate rows in the spec, ZERO state a pH, and the 3 that state Mg (Pollard 1986) state 1 mM TOTAL MgCl2 at 22 C in 50 mM KCl (ionic strength ~53 mM), not 0.5 mM FREE Mg at 150 mM. So the transfer error in those rows is UNBOUNDED by anything in this file; what is bounded here is only this engine's sensitivity. Closing that needs the sources read and their conditions written into the rows (a KB item, INVENTORY E' P3)

Two bounds put the value here: (i) self-consistency with crosslink.k_off0 — the resting thermal load sqrt(k_BT k) must be << f_char = k_BT/x_beta, i.e. k << f_char^2/k_BT = 5.7e4 pN/um (at 4.6e5 every bond carried 44 pN rms at rest, Bell x17, and 58 % tore in 10 us on RESULT-2026-09-11-motor-occupancy); (ii) the step — a 4.4-nm thermal kick at dt 1e-6 must not push the Bell exponent past 1: k <= 3.5e3. Molecule: 8 spectrin repeats per rod, folded-repeat stiffness ~1700 pN/nm each (Paramore 2005 MD), flexible terminal regions (Golji 2009), and the repeats UNFOLD at 25-35 pN (Rief 1999 JMB 286:553) below the 40-80 pN bond rupture. DESIGN ITEM (PI 17:11): the crosslink as a YIELDING element — this stiffness up to f_y ~25-35 pN, then ~30 nm of unfolded extension per repeat, refolding < 1 s on release (a bonds/builder change); until then this elastic element is the stand-in

What the OK-verdict evidence constrains is the SUM envelope+lamina: Stephens 2017 MBoC 28:1984 (10.1091/mbc.E16-09-0653, audit OK) single-nucleus micromanipulation gives a short-extension spring 0.41-0.70 nN/um with 1.5-2.5x strain stiffening carried by lamin-A/C, i.e. a lamin-attributable 2.5e2-7.5e2 pN/um for a somatic mammalian nucleus (a shell spring k ~ C*mu, C = O(1) — order of magnitude, not a modulus).
